title: Comparing Surface Syntax Variants by Token Overhead
description: Tokenize Python-style and C-style versions of the same program and compare their punctuation, keyword, and identifier token counts.

steps.description: Define PROGRAM_A (Python-style colons and indentation) and PROGRAM_B (C-style parentheses, braces, and semicolons) expressing the exact same program.
Compile a master regex in tokenize_simple(source, style) to classify tokens into KW, ID, NUM, STR, OP, PUNC, and NL while skipping whitespace, and tokenize both programs.
Print both token streams and call syntax_overhead(tokens) to count PUNC, KW, and ID tokens for Variant A and Variant B.

steps.question: Which metric in syntax_overhead differs between PROGRAM_A and PROGRAM_B, and why do keywords and identifiers stay identical?
steps.answer: Only 'punctuation' differs (3 colons in Variant A vs. 16 parentheses, braces, and semicolons in Variant B); both programs use the exact same 6 keywords and 8 identifiers.

steps.description: Review how the target audience and niche determine whether fewer punctuation tokens or familiar C-style delimiters are the better tradeoff.
Watch tokenize_simple append (kind, val) pairs as master.finditer scans PROGRAM_A.
